quest.title: Tears Among the Leaves
quest.description: You take a stroll while taking in the scenery for poetic inspiration. As you share your verses with each other, there seems to be a faint sense of sorrow amidst the joyful laughter...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, everyone got here so early.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The sun is shining bright today! As soon as that leaf floats past Stone Gate, we shall reveal today's poetry theme!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: The theme of the second day of the "Neighboring Nations Congenial Poetry Gala" is... Pairing couplets!

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: (Pairing couplets? I've heard of that — it's a Liyue art form where you have to create new lines of poetry based on fixed rules. Kind of like... a fill-in-the-blanks game, but for poetry?)

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Heaven and earth, rain and wind, the endless sky and the boundless land. Forest boars and ocean shrimp, Lavender Melons and Matsutake 'shrooms!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Based on a given line of poetry, you must create the second line to form a pair, or "couplet"! As long as you take inspiration from the wide world around you, you'll find it's not so difficult after all.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: The two lines should be neatly matched, complementing each other both semantically and rhythmically. In essence, it's just like most other forms of poetry.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: To buoy your imaginations and allow the winds of inspiration to fill your sails, we've added an additional component: an inspiration walk!

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: (...An "inspiration walk"?)

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: By inspiration walk, we simply mean wandering around in the wild, taking in the scenery, and pocketing any poetic thoughts.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Of course, to all our friends, old and new, please be careful while out and about. Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is already fully booked for the month ahead, and if there's any more demand, I'll be the only one with a smile on my face.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: In short, please roam freely as the mood takes you, enjoy the spectacular scenery of our two beautiful nations, and fill your imaginations with the most pleasing of poetry! We will all reconvene here tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, can you round up Xingqiu, Chongyun, and the Mondstadt contingent? I have a favor to ask of you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, is it that thing from yesterday?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No problem.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, thanks, I'm counting on you!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You gather the team, and briefly describe what's really going on...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: So, we hope that each of you can keep an eye out for this while you're out on your inspiration walk.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Are you sure this is okay? It was just something I ran into, and now we're imposing my business on everyone else...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Please don't say that, Mr. Chongyun. Master Jean ordered us to work with you however we can to improve cooperation. Helping each other out is exactly what we're here for.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Besides, investigating any strange occurrences near Mondstadt and making a report to the Knights of Favonius is also part of our job.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: I don't mind either. 'Cause while we're out, I can look for new cocktail ingredients too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, just think of it like an outing with friends. It'll be fun!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No need to feel bad.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: The way I see it, you should just humbly accept their willingness to help.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Alright, in that case, thank you all very much. I will be sure to repay your kindness some day.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Now, how about we split into two groups for the day?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: You mean, to cover more ground?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Not just that. Don't forget, this is still part of the poetry gala!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: If we all see the same sights and sounds during our inspiration walk, how can we write unique poems?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: That's true... but how do we decide who goes in which group?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Why don't we draw lots?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Hehe, that'll make things even more fun.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: (Drawing lots!? But what if I end up with the Liyue crowd, and I can't think of anything to say to them?)

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I've got the slips of paper here. Who wants to go first?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon! Paimon wants to go first!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone draws a lot...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #Okay, so that's {NICKNAME}, Paimon, Diona, and Chongyun in one group, and Xingqiu, Mika, and Noelle in the other.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: (What a relief... at least I'll have Noelle with me...)

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Then I humbly place myself at your instruction.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Oh... Uh, I don't think... That won't be...

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I also await your guidance.

choices.text: No need to be so formal, man.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Take care, everyone. See you all tonight!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Did anyone forget to bring anything? If not, then let's get going! C'mon!

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: (Wow... are those ears and tail real? So fluffy...)

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: Alright. Miss Diona, is there someplace in particular you would like to go?

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Just call me Diona! Since we're trying to find that thing you saw, why don't we start with the place you saw it last time?

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: Sure. Then, everyone follow me.

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: Captain? Hey, quit messing around.

choices.text: Taking a stroll, that's the plan.

talks.objective: Follow Chongyun to the location of the incident

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Right over there, next to the water. That's where I saw it. But it was a little foggy at the time, so I didn't get a clear look.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Uhh... The view from here's great, but there's kind of a gloomy atmosphere around here. Is this the kind of place you like to take a walk?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I wasn't taking a walk. I come here to train.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Train? Like how knights train for combat?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Um, it's a bit different. As an exorcist of Liyue, my training involves practising techniques for the exorcism of evil spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Exorcism?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I've always wanted to demonstrate the power of exorcism, but... it's a pity, I've never actually gotten the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chongyun is one-in-a-million: He has a pure-yang spirit! So, as soon as he gets close, evil spirits run and hide!

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Huh? Isn't that a good thing?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: It's awful! Have you ever heard of an exorcist that's never seen an evil spirit? A lot of people think I'm a fraud because of this condition of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Your physical constitution is far rarer than the techniques still passed down by exorcists today. You should treasure it.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Conqueror of Demons?

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Is that a friend of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! This is Xiao, an Adeptus of Liyue!

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: (An adeptus? Wow! I've never seen one of those before!)

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Uh... Hello, Mr. Adeptus.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Just call me Xiao.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Sooo... are you here to train too? Or are you out for an inspiration walk?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...When I heard about the exorcist's encounter, my suspicions were roused. That's why I'm here.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I've already informed the owner of the inn. If you see anything out of the ordinary, return immediately and leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I, um... aw, I'm really sorry. I didn't mean to drag even the Conqueror of Demons into this...

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I have already patrolled the area and found nothing amiss. Either the anomaly you encountered was no evil spirit, or perhaps it already left.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I guess that means we came all this way for nothing...

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: If there's no other business, I'll be taking my leave now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you should come! There's no one else around here anyway, so you don't need to worry.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: But...

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: I would also be honored if you joined us, Adeptus Xiao. It is a rare opportunity, and... I have many questions about exorcising evil spirits that I would like to ask you.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Fine.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: (Seems like this adeptus is pretty shy... or maybe all the adepti in Liyue are like this?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Team Chongyun has a new member, yay!

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: Wh—What? When did this become my team? Now that Adeptus Xiao is joining us, if anyone's team leader, it should be—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't overthink it! Diona, didn't you say you wanted to find some new ingredients?

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Yeah. I don't get to come to Liyue very often, so I wanna gather some new ingredients while I'm here!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: I've heard that Liyue's Jueyun Chilis can set your throat on fire! Is that true? I'm gonna mix them into my drinks and give it a try!

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: (Huh? Jueyun Chilis?)

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: Um... I'm not sure that would taste very good...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Really? Purrfect! Let's go pick a whole bunch of 'em!

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: What the...?

choices.text: Come on an inspiration walk with us!

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Have fun, you two. I'll have the tent set up soon.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: With this wood and the food I brought along, we can definitely put together a decent lunch.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: You've got quite a knack for wilderness survival, I'll give you that.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Thanks! I... I was on an expedition with the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius for a while not too long ago. I was in charge of surveying and mapping.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Oh? You sound like a character from an adventure novel, charging across the world, sword in hand!

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Wha...? No, I'm nowhere near as amazing as all that...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: If I really run into a powerful enemy, I always leave it for someone stronger to deal with...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: You're too modest, Mika. A hero is measured not by the blood on his sword, but by what's in his heart.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: As long as a righteous heart that yearns to aid others beats within your chest, no matter where you go, or what you have achieved, you may be called a "hero."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: (That all sounded pretty profound... I've never even thought about any of that before.)

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: (He must be one of Liyue's great martial arts heroes! I wish I could express myself as clearly and confidently as he can...)

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Hello? Are you okay? Maybe we should return, lest Noelle be forced to wait on us.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Oh, sure.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: There's a poem written on it. The Conqueror of Demons has truly amazing vision...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... It sounds like the author is writing about the first time they met their true love...

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Although the following lines suggest that they didn't end up together.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...Why write a poem on a fallen leaf?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: The flowing waters are ruthless — they carry the leaves away with the current. This poem would likely have vanished into the void had we not found it.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...It makes no sense to me.

choices.text: Sometimes, people write poems simply to express themselves.

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: That's true. I've heard Xingqiu say something similar before.

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: When there's things that you're unable to say, or just never had the chance to say before it was too late... If it can be put on paper, it can be expressed as poetry.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Is it kinda like wishing at a fountain? I used to do that sometimes when I was little.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... That means that our mystery poet was probably hoping that someone would read it, right?

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: You think? Then... Should we write a poem in reply?

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: But we don't know who wrote it. How can we reply?

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: ...Why not go upstream?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Upstream? Why?

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: The ink looks fresh. It can't have been written too long ago.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: This withered leaf floated down with the current. If we travel further upstream and drop a leaf into the same waters, it should be carried down past the original writer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cool! Ah, this is so romantic — communicating with a mystery person using poems on fallen leaves!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: But how do we make sure that they'll receive it?

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: We can write extra copies and drop the leaves in different places! As they say, where there's a will, there's a way. Surely at least one of our leaves will find a path?

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Either way, it's our only option.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then let's make like a tree and head upstream!

choices.text: It doesn't matter if anyone else reads it.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Okay, this should be enough!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: ...Diona, you seem really committed to, uh... making alcoholic drinks available to people of all tastes.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: What!? No! Never! I HATE alcohol!

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: When grown-ups drink too much, they get that stupid drunk look on their faces, can't speak clearly, and don't even respond properly! Sometimes they just sleep on the floor all night! Alcohol is the root of all kinds of evil...

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: So I'm on a mission to mix the most disgusting drink in the whole world, and show everyone just how awful alcohol really is! Nothing can stand in my way — if it means coming out to Liyue every day to pick fresh Jueyun Chilis, then so be it, hmph!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Um... Is it really worth all that effort?

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Uh, yeah! 'Cause all my previous efforts have failed... Those stinkin' boozehounds not only haven't woken up to the truth of how bad alcohol is, they even keep praising my drinks! It makes me FURIOUS!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: But... how is that possible? If this is the kind of stuff you're throwing into their drinks, it must taste absolutely vile, surely?

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Are you calling me a liar!? Well, if you don't believe me, I'll fix you a drink right now, then you'll see!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Huh? Uh, no... no need, I...

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Hmph! Just you wait.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: (Oh no, is she really going to add those Jueyun Chilis?)

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...If her claims are true, perhaps she, too, possesses a unique constitution of some kind?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I don't see how it could have anything to do with her. Unless... she's under the influence of some kind of power? Maybe an evil spirit?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: No. I sense no trace of the demonic in her — although there are traces of something else. Something rather special.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: In Liyue, we might say this child has adeptal affinity.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: It's ready. Here, I made one for Xiao too.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: (Oh boy, look at that color... Yep, she definitely added Jueyun Chilis.)

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: What's wrong? You're not allergic to anything, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Don't worry, there isn't even any alcohol in it. It's a Slime Condensate base with a seasoning of Jueyun Chilis and finished with frog legs.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: (Surely, there's no way this can possibly taste good...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't force yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: (Xiao downed it in a single gulp! Ugh, great... If the Conqueror of Demons drank it, it'd be rude of me to refuse...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chongyun drank his too! Is he gonna be okay?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: This drink is...

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: ...Delicious!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: It does have a touch of Jueyun Chili, but it isn't at all overpowering! It's completely different from Xiangling's cooking or those drinks Xingqiu makes to mess with me!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: It's crisp and refreshing, with just a hint of numbness, and the Jueyun Chili flavor combines with the smooth but not slimy texture of the frog legs to form a heavenly mixture!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: And oh, the Slimes! Can we talk about the Slimes!? Before this, I never knew that they had such a pure and herby taste, like... fresh grass after the rain! The power and purity of nature, distilled into a cup! Amazing! Simply unbelievable!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Slimes are absolutely sublime!

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Ugh, I failed again... But wait... What's gotten into Chongyun? He's been so quiet up until now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I'm great! And I gotta try another — Diona, if you please, one more!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: At your instruction, Diona serves Chongyun with an ice-cold drink...

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I... *panting* ...Okay, I think I've calmed down a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I can't believe I let you all see me like that.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: It's fine. My fault for not checking your spice tolerance first.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Looks like this "pure-yang spirit" isn't such a great thing to have after all.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Actually... before I drank it, I very much doubted what you said about your drinks...

dialogues.speaker: Diona & Chongyun
dialogues.text: *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who'd have thought it... Diona and Chongyun are actually kinda similar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xiao, what's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Look over there.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: You mean the leaf?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Something's written on it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? You can see that from over here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's grab it and take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah! Or it'll get swept away!

talks.objective: Pick up the leaf in the water

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Upstream, upstream, up we go~! Oh, did you think of what to write yet?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I already finished writing it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! Now give it here, and Paimon'll toss it on the water!

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: ..."Things you never had the chance to say before it was too late"... When silence is the final word, we mourn the loss of things unheard...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You should try writing a poem too, Xiao.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: I have little talent for nor knowledge of poetry...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The leaf's in the water! Look, it's like a little boat. Merrily, merrily down the stream, life is but a dream!

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: We should probably pick up the pace. We still have a few more leaves to set afloat, and we need to get back before it gets dark.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, let's gooo... Huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's this? You two having a private chat?

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: ...No, it's nothing.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: I just hope this isn't all in vain.

choices.text: Seems like the idea of getting involved has grown on you.

talks.objective: Go on a walk to get some inspiration

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Ah, the scenery here is quite beautiful. Let's pause here to seek some inspiration.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Should we set up camp? Please wait a moment, I'll pitch the tent.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: It's an inspiration "walk," there's no need for all that...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Okay, well I'll conduct reconnaissance nearby to ensure this area is safe, and see if I can't scavenge any firewood or food while I'm at it.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Wait... reconnaissance?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: It means survey the environment and plan our route forward. It's the foundation of all operations while out in the wild.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: (Are all inspiration walks in Mondstadt this complicated...?)

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: (They're acting like this is completely normal... am I the weirdo here?)

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: In that case, I'll "conduct reconnaissance" with Mika.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh... okay then.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: (Crumbs, now I have to try and make small talk... Should I mention the scenery? The weather?)

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Very well, then leave the camp to me!

talks.objective: Go back to camp and talk to Noelle

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: You're back! Did everything go smoothly? Do you need a cloth to wipe the sweat from your brow?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: No need, thanks. All clear. There's no danger in the vicinity.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The team lights a fire and starts preparing lunch.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Before long, a delicious meal is ready.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Noelle, your cooking is amazing! Every single dish is so tasty.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Truly astounding, I never imagined it was possible to enjoy such a satisfying meal in the great outdoors.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Really? Then what do you usually eat when you're out on an inspiration walk?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Oh, well, since I usually sneak out from home, I just grab some dried snacks to take with me. Add in whatever fruit I pick along the way, and that's my lunch.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: By sneaking out, you mean... running away from home?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: That's right! Or sometimes, I'll tell a cover story, like... I'm going out to take care of business.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: But... if you get caught, won't you get disciplined?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: So just don't get caught!

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: (With such a devil-may-care attitude, no wonder he seems so carefree. Maybe I should take a leaf out of his book...)

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Anyway, did anything interesting come up while you were out scouting?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Well, Xingqiu and I talked about what it means to be a "hero."

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Now that I think about it, by Xingqiu's definition, you should be considered a hero too, Noelle!

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Huh? Me?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: You're always happy to help everyone in the Knights of Favonius. Not only that, but whenever we're out training, you help out the citizens of Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Remember that time when a giant boulder was blocking the road? You cut it in two with a single blow!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Oh? Sounds like she has both a heroic spirit and incredible martial prowess.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Don't... Please don't praise me like that! ...We should talk about what we came here to do: finding inspiration.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Miss Hu Tao said something about pocketing our... poetic thoughts. But so far all we've done is gather some firewood and cook lunch. I have no idea what to write...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: You can write about anything.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Looking at Cor Lapis, one can't help but wonder if one's own heart is as bright and clear as jade. Observing silk, so bright and beautiful, one pauses to consider whether it ever feels the sadness and sorrow that humans do.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: So, we have to connect our internal world with the external one?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Exactly! But that's just one of many possible methods.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Perhaps you might gaze out at the bridge in the distance, and see a woman leaning on the railing, looking as if her heart is laden by sorrows that even the rushing waters below cannot wash away...

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, I saw her at the gala yesterday. She wrote one of the riddles we answered.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Why don't we go say hi?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Enjoy your inspiration walks! I'm looking forward to some splendid poetry tonight.

talks.objective: Talk to the woman on the bridge

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Hello, Ma'am. How fortuitous it is that we meet again.
Hello. Are you here on your inspiration walk too?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Yes. Allow me to introduce ourselves: I am Xingqiu, and this is Noelle and Mika.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Thank you for accepting our answer to your riddle yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Callirhoe
dialogues.text: Oh, don't mention it. It's all in good fun. I'm Callirhoe.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: ...So, Miss Callirhoe, are you from Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Callirhoe
dialogues.text: That's right! I was traveling in the area, and just happened to see there was a poetry event being held at Stone Gate. It looked fun, so I thought I'd drop in.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Your riddle yesterday made quite an impression on me. It was uniquely evocative. Have you studied Liyue poetry before?

dialogues.speaker: Callirhoe
dialogues.text: I haven't, actually. I've just picked up a few things here and there from chatting with people throughout my travels.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Amazing! So you're a natural poet!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: We noticed you standing on the bridge from quite some distance away. Are you drawing poetic inspiration from the flowing current beneath your feet?

dialogues.speaker: Callirhoe
dialogues.text: Haha, I haven't finished my poem yet. The water here was just so peaceful and calming, I stopped for a moment and lost myself in admiring it...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Well, since we're all here, why not head back with us to the venue for tonight's festivities? It's getting late, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Callirhoe
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Are... Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: We can walk and talk. Perhaps the mingling of ideas will give rise to new inspiration.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: I'd personally like to hear Miss Callirhoe's couplet. I'm sure I can learn something.

dialogues.speaker: Callirhoe
dialogues.text: Haha, well if you're all in agreement, I've got no reason not to join you.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Woohoo, the first team is back, right on schedule!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Huh? The others have yet to return?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...C'mon, let's hurry!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: *wheezing* We... *panting* ...We're not too late, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Just how far did you all go?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, everyone catch your breath... Come on, deep breaths, one... two. Now don't panic, the party hasn't started yet!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... We made it... Paimon's exhausted...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Since when do you get tired from flying...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets tired if she has to fly too fast!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not to mention dropping all those leaves. Paimon's hands are cramping up...

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Hmph! Sounds like someone needs to exercise more.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You guys picked up a new teammate while you were out?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Indeed. This is Callirhoe — I believe you'll remember her from yesterday, though you weren't introduced.

dialogues.speaker: Callirhoe
dialogues.text: Hi everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello! But you're not the only ones who called in reinforcements! Hee-hee, look who we got...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Xiao? Where'd he go?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: XIAOOOOOO! Come on oooout~!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ahem, now that we've all regrouped, let's... Huh. Scratch that, looks like we're still waiting on my co-host.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hohoho, they say roosters crow at first light, and finches go to bed at night, but Director Hu Tao's always on the ball — anytime, anywhere, she'll answer your call!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Are the theatrics really necessary? We're already on day two of the festival. The opening ceremony is over...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh ho, but my dear dear Paimon, it seems you are not yet aware. That was not for my own sake, but for a special guest who is joining us today—

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Director Hu's manner is as exuberant as ever. It always makes quite an impression.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oh boy, now this is a surprise!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Mr. Zhongli, I hope you are well.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Xingqiu... What can you tell me about Mister Zhongli? He seems like somebody very important.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Yes — he's held in very high regard in Liyue Harbor. He's extremely erudite in many different domains of knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Allow me to introduce you all to Zhongli, a consultant at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: His expertise is limitless, stretching from the celestial orbs to the terrestrial ores, spanning modern and ancient culture, delving into literature both prosaic and poetic.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: He may be my subordinate, but he is certainly a qualified poetry expert. And so, we have invited him here tonight to judge the compositions.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The director exaggerates. I am but vaguely acquainted with a few lines of classical poetry. Should you consider me to be remiss in my appraisal of your own compositions, please correct me.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Aiya, enough with the modesty already! If I didn't know better, I'd say you seemed nervous. Just focus on judging.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Please rest assured that I shall rise to the occasion, Director.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Let me do a quick count... one, two, three, four... Great, equal numbers on both sides.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you counting me, too?

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Okay, fine... But consider this a favor!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hmm, with our Fontaine friend present, perhaps we should rename this event to the "Three Nations Congenial Poetry Gala"...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #Also, I'm just noticing that Paimon should only count as a half-teammate at most...? Hmm, that kinda puts Team {NICKNAME} at a bit of a disadvantage...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Well, how about this: I'll join in as well! Director Hu Tao, here to help out in your hour of greatest need! What does everyone think?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Naturally, the more the merrier. Being the host of the festival shouldn't stop you from having the chance to enjoy it like the rest of us.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Then it's settled! Everyone else in the audience, feel free to join in too, and support your favorite team!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: What about me? Shall I keep track of the score?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: No need for that! The teams are just a formality. We're all friends here, and this isn't intended to be competitive. But what do you think, Judge Zhongli?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I concur, Director. Moreover, it would be disingenuous to impose upon our friends from Mondstadt and Fontaine a competition in which they are judged on how rigorously they can adhere to Liyue poetic conventions.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Since this is a "Congenial Poetry Gala," should we not begin with inspiration and finish with friendly conversation? The aim being for all participants to enjoy themselves.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Phew, that's a relief... I was so nervous about this, but it sounds like it's gonna be pretty relaxed...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Couldn't have asked for a better judge — Zhongli said everything I was supposed to say, only far more eloquently. So without further ado... I shall pass the baton to Venti.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: No problem.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Friends old and new, put on your thinking caps and take a deep breath of fresh air! The second stage of our poetry gala will now commence: matching couplets!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Perhaps I could break the ice with a humble contribution to inspire others to share their brilliance.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Please listen to the first line in the couplet: "Lounging in luxury inside a Xinyue Kiosk booth, delighting in countless contemporary tastes."

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: (What? He managed to think of one already? He seems like a real expert at this...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, Xinyue Kiosk... Should that be paired with Liuli Pavilion? Or are they too similar for a couplet? Ugh, this is pretty difficult!

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: (Xinyue Kiosk... contemporary tastes... Hmm, I guess I should pair the modernity of their VIP dining experience with an emblem of the past... Ah! Maybe where I was training that one time? That was quite ancient. The weather was terrible that day...)

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: ...Okay! I got something!

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: ..."Surrounded by history outside a Tianheng Pass pavilion, as lightning sets the boundless tenebrous skies ablaze."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! Chongyun completed the couplet!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Hmm... Xinyue Kiosk is a renowned modern restaurant, while the mountain pass of Tianheng is a prominent historical landmark. These two iconic locations form a complementary pair.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The imagery also contrasts rather well between the two halves of the couplet, one half describing a leisurely and comfortable indoor scene, the other portraying a hazardous outdoor scenario where there is no protection from the elements.

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: (Huh? I was just describing what I experienced that day... I guess I just got lucky?)

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: Alright then, I guess I'll start the next couplet:

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: "Mind pines for Mingyun, flesh confined to Qingce, spirit striding high on Jueyun's clouds."

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: (Oh, Chongyun, you dark horse... Looks like you came to play today...)

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: This conjures the image of one with lofty aspirations, whose life is limited to a small town, but who awaits the opportunity to one day ascend above the clouds. The use of various locations for their symbolism is quite novel indeed.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: "Soul shines like jadestone, dressed in finest silkwear, lucent heart still beats within me now."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, how did Noelle do that!?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: A superb line. It employs the metaphor of precious stone to describe one of noble and moral character, with a pure and clear heart. The symbolism in this case is centered around objects. Truly, the work of a skilled poet.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: That was a commendable couplet.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: All thanks to your guidance while we were out on our inspiration walk.

response.speaker: Callirhoe
response.text: I'd like to start the next couplet:

response.speaker: Callirhoe
response.text: "Up into the misty karst, down among the grassy marsh, all for Lotus Seed and Bird Egg Soup."

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: ...Lotus Seed and Bird Egg Soup?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is it, Diona? Did you think of a second line for the couplet?

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: No, everyone's poems are so complicated. I need more time just to understand them...

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: But when I heard "Lotus Seed and Bird Egg Soup," it made me think of Berry and Mint Burst... maybe because I mixed a similar drink recently.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "North beyond the Starfell Lake, south across the windswept plains, just for berries squeezed and mint infused."

response.speaker: Callirhoe
response.text: #No wonder everyone praises {NICKNAME} so highly! You answered so quickly.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Both halves of this couplet require intimate knowledge of the terrain in question and the local plants that may be found there. The two of you are clearly both seasoned travelers.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Does this mean I helped? Meowza!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hey now, Zhongli, don't just praise everything you hear! You should question and press them a bit, don't worry about upsetting anyone! After all, I'm here to take the heat!

response.speaker: Callirhoe
response.text: Then allow me to try another:

response.speaker: Callirhoe
response.text: "'Qingxin' has no heart, still it soothes the human heart."

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: Is she talking about the medicinal effects of Qingxin? Hmm... this is a hard one to match.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...The "xin" part of Qingxin means heart, but the flower itself has no heart...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "'Sweet Dream' is no dream, yet it nurtures people's dreams."

response.speaker: Huanxi
response.text: Sweet dream? Does that really match?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Hmm. Since the suitability of the match has been queried, I shall act according to the Director's wishes, and ask you: What is the link between "Sweet Dream" and "Qingxin"?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Sweet Dream" is a type of dessert.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhh! You mean eating a delicious dessert before bed will make you sleep well, right? You're amazing!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Actually, we sleep peacefully at night because Xiao is there to protect everyone.)

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Haha, then I agree, the two halves of the couplet match. This point is well deserved.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Points for me, points for thee, this judge gives out points for free...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: But if you ask me, everyone's being a little too conventional so far. Let's push the envelope a little! Go nuts!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Oh? In that case, why don't you finish this one for me, Hu Tao?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: "Round moon in the heavens: full moon at night, celebrate with circle of friends."

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: "Square meals in the basement: big bowls of rice, decorate with cuboids of meat."

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Huh? Wh—What the...?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Ah, we have ourselves a "pedants' couplet."

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The two halves have no thematic connection... Yet each word has its perfect parallel, meaning the two halves do form a cohesive whole. The strict pairings make this no easier to achieve than a thematically coherent couplet.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Blah blah blah! So verbose. Zhongli, just tell me if I got a point or not.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Of course, you did. I presumed it went without saying.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Ahem... "Through Qiongji I walked a hundred miles, at Guili I ended my march. In Dihua the silvergrass grows in two styles, but horsetails don't trot out the marsh."

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: "From vendors I bought some fifteen steaks, at dinner I sizzled the lot. At pressure the tenderloin cooks in two ticks, but fifteen won't fit in the pot."

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's a "pedants' couplet"? Paimon thinks she can do that too!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: I thought of one!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: "Wolfhooks can't hook Baron Bunny."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aww, that's a cute couplet!

response.speaker: Levin
response.text: "Sweet Flowers can't outsweet Sister Barbara!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Haha, now that's the passion we like to see, although... unfortunately, your response was technically one word too long.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: In that case... "Whopperflowers can't whop Jumpy Dumpty."

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Oho! This Mondstadter's got talent!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: (Phew... I'm so relieved I at least managed to get one...)

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: "Nestling by a roaring fire, scent of tea wafts from the stove, reading through the Heart of Clear Springs."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! Noelle came up with another one!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, match the couplet! Paimon knows you can do it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Why don't you try it, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh!? Do you really think Paimon has what it takes...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fine, Paimon'll give it a whirl...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Nestling by a roaring fire, scent of tea wafts from the stove, reading through the Heart of Clear Springs."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... "Seething in the pouring rain, sword of pain swipes at my foe, beating up the Eye of the Storm!"

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Great job!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Really?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Yes, very good!!! The image of challenging powerful foes in the harshest of conditions seemed to manifest before my eyes, and it was perfectly juxtaposed against the atmosphere of leisurely reading with a cup of freshly brewed tea.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: R—Really? Hehe... Maybe Paimon has a knack for this after all!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: ...It appears that my services as a judge are no longer needed.

choices.text: Match each word, one by one, and you'll be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: In high spirits, the laughter and couplets continue late into the night...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woohoo, Paimon's so happy! Paimon managed to match a bunch of couplets at the end! You did hear them all, right?

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: I really enjoyed myself too! I never knew Liyue's couplet poetry was so much fun.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You were amazing today, Noelle! You did so many couplets.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon especially liked your one about reading "Heart of Clear Springs." Paimon never could've thought of that!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Callirhoe?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Miss Callirhoe, are you okay? You look like you're getting tired.

dialogues.speaker: Callirhoe
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm fine. Thanks for asking.

dialogues.speaker: Callirhoe
dialogues.text: Although... I do have a question I'd like to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Callirhoe
dialogues.text: Have all of you read "Heart of Clear Springs"?

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: I haven't actually read it.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: My dad told me the story once. It's about a spring fairy and a young boy.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Oh yes, the story of a spring fairy who left her homeland, and met a boy under the moonlight in a faraway land.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: The boy poured out his heart to her, and she listened to his stories.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Over time, the boy grew up, and began to develop feelings for the spring fairy. But the spring fairy didn't understand human love, and was afraid that making a promise to him would ultimately end in tragedy... and so... um...

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: (I don't know if Diona's father mentioned the part about the kiss to her...)

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: In the end, the spring fairy left the boy, and was never heard from again.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Ah, yes, that's it! Many years went by, and the boy became an old man, but he never stopped believing that the fairy was real, and not just a dream.

response.speaker: Chongyun
response.text: Sounds like a tragic tale...

response.speaker: Callirhoe
response.text: So, what do you guys think of the spring fairy in the story?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I'm sure she made her decision with the best of intentions, but the boy couldn't hope to understand why she left... It's a shame that the misunderstanding never got cleared up.

response.speaker: Callirhoe
response.text: Well... Do you think she should go back and see that boy again, if she ever had another chance?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now? But... isn't he an old man by the end of the story?

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Hmm... isn't it a bit late? What if it just led to more regrets?

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Ah! Sorry, maybe I'm being too pessimistic...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Paimon was that boy... Hmm, actually, Paimon would definitely want to see the spring fairy again. No matter how old Paimon got. After all, she's the love of his life, right?

response.speaker: Callirhoe
response.text: I see...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Oh? Looks like the party's still going strong over here. Are you coming up with more couplets? Need my help?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Stick to hosting, Tone-Deaf Bard! If you get involved, you'll only match every couplet yourself and not leave any for the rest of us!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Haha, I never knew you had such a high opinion of my abilities, Paimon.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But the couplet games are all over now! Tomorrow's theme is "Freestyle Poetry"!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Do we have to share our own poems with everyone?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That's right! If you're not feeling confident, don't worry — it's never too late to register for Venti's Poetry Cram Class.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: I'll sign up!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Me too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on, buster... Before you start peddling your classes, just how much freedom is there with this freestyle poetry, exactly? Aren't there any requirements at all?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: It's as free as the winds that blow, and there's nothing freer! There are no limits to genre, form, content, or anything else. So long as it comes from the heart, you're welcome to put it into poetry.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Give it a try, there's no better chance to express your innermost thoughts!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Whoa... That's almost too much freedom! Paimon can't decide which way to go... Our travels? Or maybe all the food that {NICKNAME} has cooked for Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Will you come too, Callirhoe? Paimon wants to see what you write!

response.speaker: Callirhoe
response.text: Oh, um... Yes. I'll be there.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Oof, my nose is starting to itch again... Alright, I shall leave you to privately ponder your poems and bid you all goodnight! See you tomorrow!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: As the host declares the day's events over, the crowd reluctantly disperses...

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: As well as Jueyun Chilis, I also need some Slime Condensate or Loach Pearls.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Are those really fit for human consumption? This is starting to sound like something Xiangling would make...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: So, Xingqiu... Uh, d—do you, um, go on inspiration walks often, or...?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I do. I always get bored when I'm cooped up at home, so I head out for a stroll.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Life gets busy. You have to steal a moment of leisure when you can.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Cool... Oh! Over there! Firewood!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The group walk back to the venue, laughing and joking as they go.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Some time ago, in a team far, far away...
